topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes, relates the content to prior histopathology practicals, and outlines the core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogenes, and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: They trace how the study of tumor viruses revealed that cancer originates from altered normal cellular genes and explain the experimental assays used to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and mechanistic actions of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: They define the functional classifications of cancer-associated genes and examine how mutations in these genes alter cell cycle checkpoints and protein function.

topics.label: Mechanisms, origins, and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the distinctions, underlying repair and replication defects, and cellular stress consequences associated with sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how the stepwise accumulation of somatic mutations and inherited germline defects drive tumor progression and accelerate malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: It wraps up the lecture, provides recommended reading, and previews the next lecture topic.
